s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive, symmetric lower extremity weakness with urinary retention and cranial nerve involvement
salient_findings: Subacute, progressive, symmetric lower extremity weakness
Nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots
key_facts: MRI brain and orbits showed no abnormality
MRI spine showed nodular thickening and enhancement of lumbosacral nerve roots
Diffuse heterogeneous signal abnormalities within bone marrow
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed elevated white blood cell count
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed elevated red blood cell count

raw.syndrome_frame: Progressive, symmetric lower extremity weakness with urinary retention and cranial nerve involvement
salient_findings: Subacute, progressive, symmetric lower extremity weakness
Nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots
key_facts: MRI brain and orbits showed no abnormality
MRI spine showed nodular thickening and enhancement of lumbosacral nerve roots
Diffuse heterogeneous signal abnormalities within bone marrow
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed elevated white blood cell count
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed elevated red blood cell count

raw.rationale: The presence of violaceous cutaneous lesions (leukemia cutis), severe flaccid quadriparesis, reduced muscle stretch reflexes, and cerebrospinal fluid analysis showing 98% atypical cells/blasts are highly suggestive of leukemia, and the subacute progression of symptoms and diffuse heterogeneous signal abnormalities within bone marrow are more consistent with acute myeloid leukemia.

rejected.label: Plasma cell leukemia
rejected.why: The presence of 98% atypical cells/blasts in the cerebrospinal fluid is not typical for plasma cell leukemia, which usually involves plasma cells.

rejected.label: POEMS syndrome
rejected.why: While POEMS syndrome can cause nerve root thickening and enhancement, the presence of leukemia cutis and 98% atypical cells/blasts in the cerebrospinal fluid is not characteristic of this condition.

rejected.label: Leukemia cutis
rejected.why: Leukemia cutis is a symptom, not a diagnosis, and the patient's other symptoms and laboratory results suggest a more systemic disease, such as acute myeloid leukemia.

rejected.label: Multiple myeloma
rejected.why: The presence of 98% atypical cells/blasts in the cerebrospinal fluid and the subacute progression of symptoms are not typical for multiple myeloma, which usually involves plasma cells and has a more chronic course.
